pumac-2023-geometry-a-07.title: Trigonometric computation
pumac-2023-geometry-a-07.body:
Here $a=4$, $b=2\sqrt3$, $c=2$, $s=3+\sqrt3$, area $2\sqrt3$, so the inradius is $r=\frac{2\sqrt3}{3+\sqrt3}$ and $r^2=4-2\sqrt3$.

Relabel $D=A_0,E=B_0,F=C_0$ and consider $T_B$. Let $B_1=FE\cap\omega_C$ (second point) and $B_2=DE\cap\omega_A$. Let $r_A,r_B,r_C$ be the radii of $\omega_A,\omega_B,\omega_C$; then $r=2r_A\sin\frac A2$ etc., and $EF=2r\cos\frac A2$, $DF=2r_B\sin B$.

The key fact is the spiral similarity $\triangle DFB_1\sim\triangle DII_C$ ($I_C$ the center of $\omega_C$), giving $FB_1=\frac{I I_C}{DI}\cdot DF=\frac{r_C}{r}\cdot2r_B\sin B=\frac{r\cos(B/2)}{\sin(C/2)}$. Then
$$EB_1=FB_1-EF=\frac{r}{\sin\frac C2}\left(\cos\tfrac B2-2\cos\tfrac A2\sin\tfrac C2\right)=\frac r{\sin\frac C2}\sin\left|\tfrac{A-C}{2}\right|,$$
and by symmetry $EB_2=\frac r{\sin\frac A2}\sin\left|\frac{A-C}2\right|$. Since $\angle B_1EB_2=90^\circ-\frac B2$,
$$[T_B]=\tfrac12EB_1\,EB_2\cos\tfrac B2=\frac{r^2}{8}\cdot\frac{\sin B-\tfrac12(\sin2A+\sin2C)}{\sin\frac A2\sin\frac B2\sin\frac C2}.$$
Summing cyclically,
$$[T_A]+[T_B]+[T_C]=\frac{r^2}{8}\cdot\frac{\sin A+\sin B+\sin C-\sin2A-\sin2B-\sin2C}{\sin\frac A2\sin\frac B2\sin\frac C2}.$$
For $(A,B,C)=(90^\circ,60^\circ,30^\circ)$: $\sin\frac A2\sin\frac B2\sin\frac C2=\frac1{\sqrt2}\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac{\sqrt3-1}{2\sqrt2}=\frac{\sqrt3-1}8$, and the numerator is $\left(1+\tfrac{\sqrt3}2+\tfrac12\right)-\left(0+\tfrac{\sqrt3}2+\tfrac{\sqrt3}2\right)=\frac{3-\sqrt3}2$. So the sum is
$$\frac{r^2}8\cdot\frac{8}{\sqrt3-1}\cdot\frac{3-\sqrt3}2=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}r^2=\frac{\sqrt3}2(4-2\sqrt3)=2\sqrt3-3=\sqrt{12}-3.$$
So $m=12,n=3$ and $m+n=15$. (A coordinate computation of the three triangles gives total area $0.4641=\sqrt{12}-3$.)

**Answer: 15**

pumac-2023-geometry-a-08.title: Recognize the configuration, then coordinates
pumac-2023-geometry-a-08.body:
The circle $\omega$ is tangent to lines $AB,AC$ and to $\ell$ on the far side of $BC$, so $\omega$ is the **incircle of $\triangle AXY$**; $D,E$ are its touch points on $AX,AY$, $F$ is its touch point on $XY$, and $\Omega=(ADE)$ is the circle with diameter $AI$ ($I$ the incenter). Also $AXY\sim ABC$ with ratio $4$, so $AX=16$, $AY=14$, $XY=18$. Everything scales by $2$ from the triangle with $XY=9$, $AY=7$, $AX=8$; compute there and multiply $PZ^2$ by $4$.

In the half-size picture put $X=(0,0)$, $Y=(9,0)$. Then $A=\left(\frac{16}3,\frac{8\sqrt5}3\right)$ (from $AX=8,AY=7$), the area is $12\sqrt5$, $s=12$, $r=\sqrt5$, $XF=s-AY=5$, so $F=(5,0)$, $I=(5,\sqrt5)$. The circumradius is $R=\frac{21}{2\sqrt5}$ with $\cos A=\frac27$, so the circumcenter is $\left(\frac92,\frac{3}{\sqrt5}\right)$. The perpendicular bisector $x=\frac92$ meets the circumcircle at the arc midpoints $\left(\frac92,\frac3{\sqrt5}\mp R\right)$; the one closer to $F$ is $P=\left(\frac92,-\frac{3\sqrt5}2\right)$.

The ray from $P$ through $F$ is $P+t\,(\tfrac12,\tfrac{3\sqrt5}2)$, with $|(\tfrac12,\tfrac{3\sqrt5}2)|^2=\frac{23}2$ and $t=1$ at $F$. A point $Z$ lies on $\Omega$ iff $(Z-A)\cdot(Z-I)=0$; substituting gives
$$\tfrac{23}2t^2-\tfrac{152}3t+\tfrac{105}2=0\iff t=\tfrac53\ \text{or}\ t=\tfrac{63}{23}.$$
The first intersection beyond $P$ is $t=\frac53$, so (half-size) $PZ^2=\frac{25}9\cdot\frac{23}2=\frac{575}{18}$. In the original size $PZ^2=4\cdot\frac{575}{18}=\frac{1150}9$.

$m+n=1150+9=1159$.

**Answer: 1159**
